entities.summary:
Eochaid mac Echdach was a 8th-century king of Dál Riata, a Gaelic kingdom in medieval Scotland and Ireland. He ruled from 726 to 733 CE and was the son of Eochaid mac Domangairt.

During his reign, Eochaid mac Echdach oversaw a period of significant cultural and economic growth in Dál Riata, with trade and diplomatic relations with other Gaelic kingdoms in Scotland and Ireland, as well as with the Vikings in Norway. He also played a key role in the development of the Kingdom of the Picts, a powerful Celtic kingdom that dominated much of Scotland during the Early Medieval period.

Eochaid mac Echdach's legacy extends beyond his own kingdom, as he helped to shape the medieval landscape of Scotland and Ireland. He was succeeded by his son, Eochaid Bal, who continued his father's policies and expanded Dál Riata's influence.

In the 9th century, Eochaid mac Echdach was remembered as a great king, and his name became synonymous with bravery and leadership. He was also celebrated for his military prowess, which he demonstrated during the Viking raids on Dál Riata.

One of the most striking aspects of Eochaid mac Echdach's legacy is the enduring impact of his reign on the cultural and linguistic heritage of Scotland and Ireland. The Gaelic language and culture, which were thriving during his reign, continue to be celebrated and preserved today.
